topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, audience background, and core learning outcomes for the cancer biology module.

topics.label: Cellular and tissue basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a failure of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic and epigenetic alterations, noting the methods and limitations involved in studying these processes.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how benign and malignant tumors differ in their capacity for invasion and metastasis, illustrating the stepwise progression from pre-malignant lesions to invasive cancer.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions used to name and classify tumors according to their tissue of origin and malignancy.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the anatomical, physiological, and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause clinical illness and patient death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor incidence across human demographics and diverse animal taxa, highlighting cancer as a fundamental vulnerability of multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Cancer screening and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical principles, efficacy, and practical challenges of population screening methods for detecting pre-invasive and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session by reviewing learning outcomes and reminding students of upcoming practical classes.
